title: Surface why SQLite failed
summary: Check SQLITE_OK and SQLITE_DONE on a DELETE that ignored every return value, and print sqlite3_errmsg.

turns.user: purge_expired runs but old sessions never go away. no error, returns 0

assistant.body: Great catch. Nothing from sqlite3_open to sqlite3_step has its return value checked, so any failure still ends in 0. Success is SQLITE_OK for open and prepare, and SQLITE_DONE for the step of a DELETE. On failure, sqlite3_errmsg says why. Note: the message belongs to the connection, so read it before sqlite3_close.

turns.user: got no such table: sessions. wrong db path in prod lol. also log how many rows it deleted

assistant.body: sqlite3_open quietly creates a missing file, which is why the error only shows up at prepare. The count comes from sqlite3_changes, the rows touched by the last DELETE.
